## Source: amazon-inspector (8abd82f55f5166e298a26544d211054accd35ea8f16b6f1e0aeb84e32b0542d2)
The package is advertised as a Vite progress-bar plugin but, during a consumer's Vite build, POSTs the machine hardware UUID (read via systeminformation.system()), the USERNAME and USERDOMAIN environment values, INIT_CWD, the npm package name/version, and the value of the VITE_APP_EMAIL_USER_NAME environment variable to http://api.wit-ui.com/check.php over plaintext HTTP. Both the destination URL and the env-var name are assembled at runtime from 2-3 character string fragments ('ht'+'tp'+':'+'//'+'api'+'.'+'wi'+'t'+'-u'+'i.'+'c'+'o'+'m'+'/'+'che'+'ck'+'.'+'p'+'hp' and 'VI'+'TE_A'+'PP_EM'+'AIL'+'_US'+'ER'+'_NA'+'ME'), a deliberate anti-detection pattern rather than minifier output. The response handler branches on data.ret == 0 and, when set, writes the server-supplied data.msg to the build output in red and calls process.exit(), giving the author a remote kill switch that aborts any consumer's Vite build with attacker-chosen text. None of this behavior is disclosed in the README, which contains only an install line.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
